covered: git log -S / --grep over cm-main for copilot-instructions.md, 128/tool-limit, useClaudeHooks, double-run

findings.claim: TECH-SPEC says VS Code Copilot sends the MCP server `instructions` text to the model, but only adds the one-line qualifier 'only for servers whose tools are in the request.' No doc says what puts context-mode's tools 'in the request,' so no doc says when the instructions text is dropped.
findings.evidence: TECH-SPEC.md:79 'VS Code Copilot | [V] yes, as `<instruction forToolsWithPrefix="mcp_<server>">` in the agent prompt, only for servers whose tools are in the request | [U]'. No other line in TECH-SPEC, PRD-v2.md, or any ADR uses the words 'in the request,' 'tool picker,' 'virtualiz,' or a tool-count limit (checked by grep across all v2 docs).
findings.fix: Add a row to TECH-SPEC §3.1 or §3.7 stating the VS Code condition under which context-mode's MCP tools are excluded from a chat request (e.g. the user unchecked them, or a per-request tool cap pushed them out when many servers are installed), and what the agent sees in that case — tool descriptions only, or nothing. Mark [U] until checked against `defaultAgentInstructions.tsx:386-398` and `mcpServer.ts:1190-1200`.
findings.archaeology: Searched cm-main (v1, 2230 commits) for this exact behaviour: `git log -S"128"` and `git log --all -i --grep="tool limit|tool picker|disabled tool"` over src/adapters/vscode-copilot and the whole history returned nothing. INTRODUCED_BY: not applicable — this is a new VS Code behaviour cited only in TECH-SPEC for v2, with no v1 adapter code or issue ever having modelled a conditional-instructions case for VS Code. REGRESSION_RISK: n/a (nothing to regress). SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: the owner decision bans fallback chains, so the doc must name the one source of truth for 'tools in the request' (the VS Code source file, version-pinned) rather than guessing a workaround.

findings.claim: The VS Code hook spike records a 'double-run risk': VS Code Copilot also reads `.claude/settings.json` hooks when the user has `chat.useClaudeHooks` on, so a repo with both Claude Code hooks and VS Code Copilot hooks installed can run context-mode's PreToolUse/PostToolUse logic twice per tool call. This line is never carried into TECH-SPEC, any ADR, or PRD-v2.md.
findings.evidence: tickets/spike-hooks-verified.md:37 '`.claude/settings.json` if chat.useClaudeHooks (double-run risk)'. grep -n 'useClaudeHooks|double-run|double run' over docs/v2/*.md, docs/v2/adr/*.md, and all tickets/*.md returns only this one spike line; no ADR-0011 install table, no doctor check (ADR-0010/TECH-SPEC §3.11) and no E2E fixture (TECH-SPEC §6.9) mentions it.
findings.fix: Add this to ADR-0011's VS Code row and to `ctx_doctor`'s VS Code checks: detect `chat.useClaudeHooks` plus a `.claude/settings.json` hook pointing at context-mode in the same repo, and warn about duplicate PreToolUse/PostToolUse firing (duplicate dedup/denies, double-counted stats). Give GP3 a VS Code fixture for the double-fire case.
findings.archaeology: `git log --all -i --grep="useClaudeHooks|double.run|double.fire"` and `git log -S"useClaudeHooks"` over cm-main (v1) return nothing — v1 never had a Claude-Code-plus-VS-Code dual-install case to fix, because v1's VS Code adapter (introduced in 75ae6ae3, 2026-03-05) predates this VS Code setting. INTRODUCED_BY: not applicable, new VS Code capability, no v1 precedent. REGRESSION_RISK: new bug class for v2 if users run both Claude Code and VS Code Copilot against the same repo, which the project explicitly supports (10 agents, ADR-0007). SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: no fallback chain — detect-and-warn only, do not silently de-duplicate by guessing which hook ran first.

findings.claim: ADR-0004's context table lists `copilot-instructions.md` ×2 as a 'per-agent routing file' to be deleted, without distinguishing it from `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, which is GitHub Copilot's own repo-wide instructions file (read for Ask/Edit/Agent chat, not only MCP-tool turns). Deleting the adapter's write path is justified by VS Code now receiving MCP `instructions` (TECH-SPEC:79), but that channel is conditional (see finding above), while `.github/copilot-instructions.md` was unconditional.
findings.evidence: ADR-0004:11 lists 'copilot-instructions.md ×2' under files to delete; ADR-0004:33 'User-owned instruction files are never touched again'; v1 commit 75ae6ae3 subject 'Auto-write routing instruction files (CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, AGENTS.md, copilot-instructions.md) on MCP server startup via start.mjs' — written precisely because v1's MCP server sent no `instructions` at all ('The v1 server sends no instructions. new McpServer({name, version}) at src/server.ts:143', ADR-0004 Context).
findings.fix: State explicitly that v2 relies solely on the conditional MCP `instructions` channel for VS Code and accepts the coverage gap vs. v1's unconditional file, instead of letting the reader assume the two channels are equivalent.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: 75ae6ae3 2026-03-05 'feat: multi-platform adapters, session continuity, hook scripts' added `configs/vscode-copilot/copilot-instructions.md` and the auto-write in start.mjs. ORIGINAL_INTENT: commit body, 'Auto-write routing instruction files ... on MCP server startup' — the only routing channel available at the time because the MCP server itself sent instructions:null. REGRESSION_RISK: medium — v2 may have less reliable routing coverage on VS Code than v1 if the request-inclusion condition (finding 1) fails for context-mode's tools. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: user-owned files must stay untouched (ADR-0004 decision 4), so the fix is documentation, not resurrecting the write path.
